correctness.rationale: For a rooted alternating matrix, the root increases rank by two exactly when its coupling row is outside the row space of the root-deleted block; this follows from a congruence splitting nondegenerate and radical parts, in all characteristics. Under a one-vertex sum the deleted blocks are independent direct summands and the row-space condition factorizes. For a rooted square the rank-zero and rank-two cases give P=1+q(q²-1)z and Q=q²+q²(q²-1)z; the resulting formula follows for every t. For odd q, the standard twisted group algebra decomposition of a class-two BCH group yields q^(3t+1-2r) characters of degree q^r for each central functional of alternating rank 2r; all field/quantifier conditions are explicit. Direct rank elimination and the separate class-size identity were checked in the embedded actual code, including t=2 and t=3.

value.rationale: Rossmann 2022 Question 1.10 explicitly motivates degree-by-degree character enumeration of graphical groups. The result gives a complete polynomial answer for a natural nontrivial infinite family of cactus (one-cut-vertex) Lie algebras, not merely another field-size sample, and supplies a rooted transfer identity that applies to arbitrary one-vertex amalgamations. It distinguishes the all-degree distribution from the previously accessible total class counts; the t=1 cycle is credited as known. The independent class-count equality is a useful consistency relation, not a substitute for the rank theorem.
